entries.content: read design/feature_descriptions/B_325_scheduler_lost_context_when_restarting_conversation.md. investigate what is happening, report your findings. Propose solution. Be short and to the point, full sentences.
I’ll trace the feature description into the relevant app and desktop conversation/scheduler paths, then report the cause and a narrowly scoped solution. I will not modify files.

---
author: 
id: B_325
internalId: 6414956f-fccd-4086-974d-cd91d67eab99
title: scheduler lost context when restarting conversation
status: design
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__6414956f-fccd-4086-974d-cd91d67eab99.json
policy:
---

I was in the middle of a conversation when the claude user account reached 100%. So I scheduled a next prompt to be sent when the account usage went back to 0.

This prompt got sent to the claude agent when the user-account -usage was reset back to 0, so far it worked. however, it did not use the previous conversation, but started a fresh new conversation which is not ok.

What needs to happen: when we schedule a new prompt for an action while the conversation was running, then the conversation needs to be continued, like normal, as is always is done when we continue an already existing conversation on a newly started agent cli

design/architecture\data_saving_and_commits.md:32:A commit-only path (`CommitRequest.paths`) is a repository path the batch stages and commits as it exists on disk at flush time; the renderer writes no content and registers no persistence outcome. It is used for desktop-written files whose content the renderer does not own, such as activity files after a conversation view-state change (`DataService.scheduleRepositoryPathCommit`). A content snapshot would be unsafe there: a running agent may write a newer activity version before the flush, and the snapshot would overwrite it. Pending entries use the key `path:<path>`, so repeated schedules for one file coalesce. The local desktop host stages each existing path with `git add` inside `ProjectOperationCoordinator` and skips paths that no longer exist. GitHub storage rejects requests with `paths`.

---
id: F-022
title: scheduled actions (timers)
status: ready
owner: JB
affects:
policy:
  checkLinting: true
  requireTests: true
internalId: 181cae82-0bf5-447b-8646-1ef33c111db1
---

## Goal

Schedule actions by stable action `id` at a date and time selected by the user. The scheduler runs in Electron and delegates execution to the same Electron action runner as manual and state-triggered runs.

## Current state

The action popup registers date/time schedules by action id. Electron persists them, restores pending timers when a project opens, and executes due schedules through the shared Electron action runner.

## implementation details

- Define a typed schedule model with schedule id, action id, context, trigger, created timestamp, and schedule status.
- Support one trigger: `at` with an absolute timestamp created from the user's local date/time selection.
- Use schedule states `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. These are separate from the execution states emitted by the action runner.
- Persist schedules as JSON in the repository so they survive restarts and project synchronization.
- Add `Schedule` before `Run` in the action popup. It opens a required date/time input and sends `{ actionId, context, trigger: { type: 'at', timestamp } }` to Electron.
- Electron owns schedule persistence and timer reconciliation so registration has one bookkeeping path.
- When a project loads, restore pending schedules and timers. When the schedule file changes, reconcile timers.
- When a schedule fires, call the Electron action runner by action id. Store the execution result and update the schedule to its terminal schedule state.
- Reject missing, invalid, and non-future timestamps during registration.
- Re-register delays beyond the platform timer limit instead of firing early.
- Surface scheduled runs through the global running-actions indicator and normal action history.
- Cancelling a pending schedule removes its timer and updates the JSON. Cancelling an already running scheduled action delegates to the Electron action runner's execution cancellation.

## acceptance criteria

- The popup shows `Schedule` before `Run` for every runnable action.
- Schedules persist action ids, not names, and survive action renaming and app restart.
- Date/time schedules fire through the single Electron action runner.
- Schedule status and action execution status remain separate.
- Pending cancellation removes the timer; running cancellation stops the Electron execution.
- Missing action ids, invalid timestamps, and invalid schedule files report visible errors without dropping other schedules.
- Tests cover date/time registration, persistence, id-based restore, timer reconciliation, long delays, runner delegation, terminal states, and both cancellation paths.

## see also

- `design\architecture\initial description\timers.md`
- `design\architecture\initial description\writings\running_actions.md`
- `design\feature_descriptions\ready\F_010c_command_execution_and_chaining.md`

- Loading files and assets.
- Writing, deleting, staging, and committing files.
- Moving files through explicit `fromPath â†’ toPath` requests.
- Emitting filesystem-watch events.
- Identifying action source JSON files.
- Scoping action contexts through `context.file`.
- Keeping `cardPath` as historical execution metadata, not ownership.
- Locating card activity through stable `cardInternalId`.
- Locking concurrent tracked actions per card path.
- Recording changed files and commit metadata.

A particularly important example is action locking: Electron constructs a `cardKey` from `rootPath + context.file`, so the cardâ€™s filepath becomes its concurrency identity: [action_worktree_execution_service.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action_worktree_execution_service.js:120).

Conversation continuation verifies stable ownership:

```text
sourceConversation.cardInternalId === currentContext.cardInternalId
```

Card activity filenames are derived from `cardInternalId`: [activity_paths.mjs](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/shared/activity_paths.mjs:22).

## Overall conclusion

There are three identity approaches in the current model:

- Cards have potentially stable `header.internalId` and user-facing `header.id`.
- Actions use stable `action.id` for execution, but `sourcePath` for editing.
- UI selection, tabs, card operations, and some Electron locks use mutable file paths; conversations and activity history use stable card identity.

Therefore, a card rename or move still affects path-based UI and execution concerns, but conversation and activity ownership remain attached through stable card identity.
â”œâ”€ Markdown files: { content, path }
â”œâ”€ Action JSON files: { content, path }
â”œâ”€ Assets: { content, contentType, encoding, path }
â”œâ”€ Schedules
â”œâ”€ Agent conversation logs
â”œâ”€ Action history logs
â””â”€ Worktree configuration
```

The important boundary is:

```text
Electron filesystem/Git
    â†’ MarkdownFile[] { content, repoRelativePath }
    â†’ preload/IPC bridge
    â†’ React DataService
    â†’ MarkdownParsingService
    â†’ ProjectCard[] / ProjectSnapshot
```

`ProjectCard`, `ProjectSnapshot`, `MarkdownFile`, and the bridge contracts are defined in [data_types.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/data/data_types.ts:46). Electron returns markdown files; React creates `ProjectCard` objects in [markdown_parsing_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/markdown_parsing_service.ts:353).

Electron retains some transient stateâ€”current project, running executions, locks, schedules, watchersâ€”but not the rendererâ€™s complete card snapshot.

## Cards versus regular markdown files

A project folder contains both cards and ordinary markdown documents. The boundary between them is hard, and it is decided by location, not by content:

- Markdown files in the **root of the working folder** are always cards. They must have an `internalId`; one is generated and persisted when missing.
- Markdown files in the **archived or releases folder** are former cards and already carry an `internalId`. A file there *without* an `internalId` is a regular markdown file.
- **Any other** markdown file in the project is a regular markdown file. It never receives an `internalId`, and loading a project must not rewrite it.

import type { SequenceBranchProgress } from './sequence_branch_progress.mjs';
import type { ActionContext } from '../app/src/data/action_context'
import type { AgentSelection } from './agent_profiles.mjs'

export const ACTION_SCHEDULES_FILE: '.md2-schedules.json'

export type ScheduleStatus = 'cancelled' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'pending' | 'running'

export interface NowScheduleTrigger {
    type: 'now'
}

export interface AtScheduleTrigger {
    timestamp: string
    type: 'at'
}

export interface AccountResetScheduleTrigger {
    agent: string
    expectedResetAt: string
    limitId: string
    type: 'account-reset'
    windowId: string
}

export interface CardStateScheduleTrigger {
    cardInternalId: string
    registrationState: string
    targetState: string
    type: 'card-state'
}

export type ScheduleTrigger = NowScheduleTrigger | AtScheduleTrigger | AccountResetScheduleTrigger | CardStateScheduleTrigger
export type ActionScheduleTrigger = Exclude<ScheduleTrigger, NowScheduleTrigger>

interface ScheduleBase {
    createdAt: string
    id: string
    status: ScheduleStatus
    trigger: ScheduleTrigger
}

export interface ActionSchedule extends ScheduleBase {
    actionId: string
    context: ActionContext
    conversationId?: string | null
    failure?: string | null
    kind: 'action'
    prompt?: string
    trigger: ActionScheduleTrigger
}

export interface SequenceSchedule extends ScheduleBase {
    agentSelection?: AgentSelection
    worktreeBranch?: string;
    branchProgress?: SequenceBranchProgress;
    actionCompleted: boolean
    actionId: string
    cardInternalIds: string[]
    conversationId?: string | null
    currentIndex: number
    currentRunId: string | null
    failure: string | null
    kind: 'sequence'
    readyState: string
    readyStateMet: boolean
}

export type Schedule = ActionSchedule | SequenceSchedule

export interface ScheduleFile {
    schedules: Schedule[]
}

export function parseScheduleFile(value: unknown): ScheduleFile
export function createScheduleFile(schedules: Schedule[]): ScheduleFile
export function parseSequenceAgentSelection(value: unknown): import('./agent_profiles.mjs').AgentSelection

entries.content:
## Findings

The scheduler loses context by design:

- The UI captures only `actionId`, context, trigger, and prompt. It does not include the current conversation identity. See [action_popup_defaults.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_defaults.ts:182).
- When the schedule fires, Electron always allocates a new conversation ID. See [action_scheduler_service.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_scheduler_service.js:660).
- The resulting runner input contains `conversationId` and `prompt`, but no `continueFrom`. Therefore, the agent executor starts a fresh conversation. See [action_scheduler_service.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_scheduler_service.js:708).
- Normal manual continuation correctly obtains the selected conversation path and passes it as `continueFrom`. See [action_popup_operations.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_operations.ts:126).
- Schedule persistence already supports an optional `conversationId`, but pending schedules do not currently use it.

## Proposed solution

When scheduling an agent prompt from an existing conversation:

1. Capture and register the current `AgentConversation.id`.
2. Persist that ID on the pending schedule.
3. When the schedule fires, derive the conversation reference from its ID and context.
4. Validate that the conversation still belongs to the same action and card and remains resumable.
5. Start the runner with `{ conversationId, continueFrom, prompt }` instead of allocating a new conversation ID.
6. Keep the current new-conversation behavior when no conversation was selected.

Tests should cover registration, persistence, runner input, terminal or missing source conversations, and unchanged command-action behavior.
